title: Unique gluing of derived maps locally in degree zero
statement:
Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\tau$ be its small etale or small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, regarded as a constant sheaf. Work in $D(T_\tau,A)$, the ordinary derived category of sheaves of $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], with cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a set-indexed Zariski open cover of $T$, with exact derived restrictions denoted by $|_{U_i}$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Let $M,N\in D(T_\tau,A)$, and assume
$$\mathcal H^a(M|_{U_i})=\mathcal H^a(N|_{U_i})=0\quad\text{for every }i\in I\text{ and }a\ne0.$$
Then $\mathcal H^a(M)=\mathcal H^a(N)=0$ for $a\ne0$, and the good-truncation maps [def-kun-truncations] induce canonical isomorphisms $M\cong\mathcal H^0(M)[0]$ and $N\cong\mathcal H^0(N)[0]$, natural in these objects and commuting with restriction. Restriction induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_\tau,A)}(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\left\{(a_i)\in\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_{D((U_i)_\tau,A)}(M|_{U_i},N|_{U_i}):a_i|_{U_i\cap U_j}=a_j|_{U_i\cap U_j}\text{ for all }i,j\right\}.$$
Under the canonical degree-zero identifications this is exactly unique gluing of the $A$-module sheaf maps $\mathcal H^0(M)|_{U_i}\to\mathcal H^0(N)|_{U_i}$. In particular equality of two such global derived maps can be checked on this cover. The assertion includes the empty scheme and its empty open cover; it asserts no gluing property for arbitrary derived complexes.

proof.text: Work directly in the fixed-ring module-valued sheaf categories of the statement [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The existing upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction identifies inverse image along each open with sectionwise localization restriction on each small site [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The jointly surjective open family is an etale covering and belongs to the pro-etale precoverage by zariskiPrecoverage_le_proetalePrecoverage. Existing localization-restriction conservativity makes these exact inverse images jointly conservative, hence jointly faithful by preservation of equalizers. Applying this to F -> 0 detects zero sheaves, including the empty cover. Applying it to each cohomology sheaf, with the exact restriction comparison, detects global concentration.

Apply [lem-pur-good-truncation-exact-normalization] to construct the canonical identifications and the explicit good-truncation roof for every heart object, and obtain bijectivity of a -> H^0(a). Its exact-functor formula gives compatibility of the normalization with open restriction. The natural cohomology comparisons transport local derived maps to maps between restrictions of H^0(M) and H^0(N). The compositor and natural-isomorphism coherence in [lem-pur-exact-derived-cohomology-coherence] proves that this transport respects the specified nested-open comparison openComp.

Glue the transported fixed-ring sheaf maps by the sheaf axiom for the presheaf of morphisms [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]: Mathlib Presheaf.IsSheaf.hom and Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff. The proof adapts the proved source Etale.Derived.HeartGluing and ProEtale.Adic.LisseCover.SheafGluing constructions to an arbitrary universe for the index family. Factor a pair of maps to U_i and U_j through their scheme-theoretic open intersection. Naturality of the local map under the resulting site-object isomorphism and the existing upperStar/localization compositor coherence convert the given intersection equality into presheaf-Hom compatibility. The sheaf amalgamation yields a global map; joint faithfulness proves uniqueness. Lift it along the H^0 bijection from Step 2. The converse compatibility follows from naturality of openComp; naturality of the cohomology comparison gives the restriction square, and the same H^0 bijection and joint faithfulness give the equality test. No boundedness or nonemptiness hypothesis is added.
